Record date: 2129-12-20
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 12/20/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Progressive shortness of breath and persistent cough with greenish sputum.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax is seen for follow-up three days post-admission for exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and suspected pneumonia. He reports minimal improvement in his respiratory symptoms despite the initiation of intravenous Levofloxacin and supplemental oxygen therapy. His cough remains productive, yielding thick greenish sputum, and he continues to experience significant dyspnea, particularly with minimal exertion. Mr. Fairfax describes his fatigue as profound, and he has had persistent fevers averaging 100.5F, contributing to his overall malaise.
The patient states he is still using Albuterol nebulizer treatments every 2 hours, which provides transient relief but does not sustain symptom control. He expresses concern regarding his lack of improvement and is anxious about potential complications.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + profound fatigue, + persistent fevers, - weight loss, - chills, + night sweats. Pulmonary - + persistent productive cough with greenish sputum, + increased wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, - orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - no joint pain. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 128/74 mmHg - Heart Rate: 82 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 30 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 88% on supplemental oxygen (2 L via nasal cannula).
General: The patient appears fatigued and is in moderate respiratory distress, utilizing accessory muscles for breathing.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Marked wheezing on auscultation; decreased breath sounds bilaterally; prolonged expiration with notable rhonchi; crackles audible throughout lung fields.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact.
Extremities: No edema; no tenderness on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation with secondary bacterial pneumonia, as evidenced by persistent respiratory symptoms and lack of clinical improvement on current treatment. 2. Persistent hypoxemia requiring ongoing supplemental oxygen; consider escalation of respiratory support if no improvement. 3. Monitor for potential complications such as respiratory failure or need for mechanical ventilation.
PLAN
1. Continue intravenous Levofloxacin 750 mg daily; reassess need for continuation based on clinical response. 2. Order a chest CT scan to evaluate for possible pulmonary embolism or abscess formation given the lack of improvement. 3. Increase supplemental oxygen to maintain saturation above 92%; consider non-invasive ventilation if oxygen saturation continues to decline. 4. Increase oral Prednisone to 40 mg daily for exacerbation management and inflammation control; reassess in 48 hours. 5. Consult Infectious Disease for evaluation of pneumonia management and potential need for additional antibiotic coverage. 6. Continue to monitor vital signs and respiratory status closely; consider transfer to the ICU if deterioration occurs. 7. Reinforce patient education regarding recognizing signs of respiratory distress and the importance of adhering to the treatment plan.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax remains hospitalized for further management of his COPD exacerbation and pneumonia. The treatment team will continue to monitor his clinical status closely, with a focus on optimizing respiratory support and addressing any complications that may arise. He is encouraged to engage in discussions regarding his care plan and to communicate any changes in his symptoms promptly.
